text:
toni (support): heads up — FundMate just opened an escalation. They say their invoice-generation flow started returning malformed JSON after the 09:15 canary. Customer says tiny prompt tweaks (a trailing period, or swapping 'total' -> 'amount') now break parsing. cc @maya

maya (support): got it. Summary from customer: previously stable for weeks. After the canary deploy to rgx-canary-3 (model: redwood-instruct-v1.2-q8_0), outputs started including extra commentary lines and occasionally omitted the 'line_items' array. They pasted two API calls (only whitespace difference) that used to produce identical JSON but now diverge.

maya (support): customer repro snippet (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-v1.2-q8_0","prompt":"Invoice for Acme Corp\nItems:\n- Widget x2\nTotal: $200","max_tokens":300}'
```
versus the same with a trailing period after Total: `$200.` — they say that second one now yields: an extra human-friendly sentence and missing line_items.

rahul (eng-runtime): thanks — tagging the canary. Which canary pool? I see rgx-canary-3 rolled at 09:12 with a kernel swap (mm-opt-2026) and a micro-quant change. Could be a decoding edge-case introduced by the new kernel or a prompt tokenization shift.

maya (support): customer reported no auth errors, no 5xx from our API gateway. Latency increased ~50ms but not enough to cause timeouts. The big user impact is broken downstream JSON parsing in their service — their pipeline fails the invoice ingestion and falls back to manual review. They quantified ~7% failure rate since deploy began, up from ~0.3%.

eli (product): this smells like a sensitivity/formatting regression. Was there any change to system prompts or instruction-tuning artifacts during model onboarding for v1.2? Also are we applying any new post-processing filters in canary?

rahul (eng-runtime): no system prompt edits in this rollout. The only changes: (1) kernel mm-opt-2026 active for short sequences, (2) slightly different default tokenization normalization (decompose punctuation in a tiny subset), (3) minor sampling temperature clamp bugfix. Any of these could alter borderline cases.

deploy-bot: rgx-canary-3 rollout started at 2026-03-15T09:12:04Z, 18% traffic.

maya (support): customer provided example diffs — copying sanitized snippets inline (they included original expected JSON and actual):
```
EXPECTED: {"invoice_id":"INV-2026-1001","line_items":[{"desc":"Widget","qty":2}],"total":"$200"}
ACTUAL: {"invoice_id":"INV-2026-1001","message":"Thanks for your order! Processing...","total":"$200"}
```
Notice line_items dropped, replaced by a free-text message.

rahul (eng-runtime): got it. That replacement implies the model sometimes injects a natural language assistant response instead of structured JSON. Possible causes: changed tokenization triggers a different conditional on the JSON boundary token, or sampling clamp makes generation more likely to take a short answer path.

eli (product): severity: high for this customer (production invoice processing). Can we repro locally on canary model? If yes, try different prompt-normalization variants to isolate tokenization sensitivity. Also need to determine rollback window.

maya (support): customer offered to run quick tests. I asked them to try an identical call but with an explicit instruction wrapper: 
"Please respond ONLY with valid JSON object with keys invoice_id, line_items, total."
They reported that wrapped instruction fixes it in 95% cases — but they can't ship that immediate change widely (too many legacy templates).

rahul (eng-runtime): I'll spin up a canary runner and reproduce. Initial plan: (1) run both tokenization traces for the two prompts, (2) generate beam/sampling debug logs, (3) toggle the normalization flag to previous version.

rahul (eng-runtime): repro steps I'm running now:
1) pull model artifact v1.2-q8_0 from canary bucket
2) run local inference with mm-opt-2026 kernel enabled
3) enable trace: REDWOOD_TRACE_TOKENS=1 and call both prompt variants 100x each
4) collect outputs + top-k logits for first 64 tokens

maya (support): customer also reported that a very tiny prompt template change — e.g., removing a colon after 'Items' — flips success/failure. That matches tokenization sensitivity. They've attached their pre- and post-templates in support ticket.

eli (product): we should consider immediate mitigation: (A) pause canary or rollback to previous kernel if repro confirms, (B) add a prompt-normalization compat layer in the API for JSON-mode requests, (C) ship a temporary best-effort post-processor that strips leading human commentary and tries to salvage line_items. Which is fastest?

rahul (eng-runtime): fastest short-term is (A) rollback kernel to mm-opt-2025 for canary pool — that's a config flip and should be <15min to rollback. (B) prompt-normalization is medium effort but doable; post-processor is brittle. I'll prepare a rollback request.

maya (support): escalation note for SRE/ops: customer impact high, customer expects ETA on fix. Requesting rollback while we investigate deeper. Customer asked for a test endpoint showing pre-rollout behavior for them to validate.

rahul (eng-runtime): starting rollback plan now. If we see failure to rollback we will route to full pool stop. Also capturing mismatch stats: after 09:12 canary start, we see a 6.9% increase in non-JSON tokens at expected JSON boundary across all customers in the canary bucket.

deploy-bot: rgx-canary-3 rollback initiated at 2026-03-15T09:40:10Z by rahul.

maya (support): updated FundMate. They appreciate quick action. They asked for a short postmortem once root cause identified and for help auditing other templates.

eli (product): next steps: - eng-runtime to confirm root cause and create minimal testcases (tokenization diffs + prompt variants) - support/customer-success to coordinate template audit and temporary template-wrapping guidance to affected customers - product to evaluate adding JSON-mode strictness flag on API (server-enforced) - ops to monitor other canary pools for similar regressions

maya (support): logging this thread into support ticket SYS-8341 and will attach the debug logs when rahul shares.

rahul (eng-runtime): quick initial finding: toggling the tokenization normalization back to previous behavior makes the 100-run A/B result go from 93/100 success on old -> 64/100 on canary to 92/100 after flip. So this points strongly to tokenization normalization change as primary culprit. I'll prepare a changelist and roll it back permanently for the next patch if agreed.

eli (product): good catch. Please include reproducible prompt pairs in the CL and add a unit test in our inference-regression suite. Also open a billing note — if customers had extra manual ops because of the regression, coordinate credits with Finance.

maya (support): FundMate confirmed behavior returned to baseline after rollback. They're back to normal. They've requested a call to review template-hardening guidance.

rahul (eng-runtime): will follow up with the exact CL and tokenization tests. Putting follow-up items in eng-runtime backlog.

maya (support): closing escalation but keeping ticket open for postmortem and template audit. :white_check_mark:
